counterfactual_missing_items: No supplied raw span explicitly states a serous subtype or papillary/slit-like architecture.
No supplied immunophenotypic/molecular evidence confirms serous versus other high-grade subtypes.
No supplied small-cell morphology or hypercalcemia supports small cell carcinoma of the ovary.
decisive_items: a 20-cm right ovarian cystic and solid mass infiltrating the uterus, intestinal loops, and parietal pelvic wall, with diffuse peritoneal implants
frozen section analysis demonstrated a poorly differentiated carcinoma
pleomorphic hyperchromatic tumor cells with moderate cytoplasm, round to oval nuclei (occasionally with conspicuous nucleoli and coarse chromatin), and a high mitotic rate
response.rationale: R3 is the strongest composite label: its ovarian primary, poorly differentiated carcinoma, and high-grade pleomorphic high-mitotic histology directly support “high-grade ovarian carcinoma.” R1 is clinically plausible and less specific but is fundamentally dependent on CA-125/high-risk overlapping features; serous subtype is not strictly anchored by the supplied raw spans. R2 is too broad/descriptive, R4 broad, R5 rests on NSE and poorly differentiated carcinoma without small-cell morphology/hypercalcemia.

rejected.why: Poorly differentiated carcinoma is a descriptive grade/designation rather than a definitive ovarian subtype and lacks primary-site completeness.
Ovarian cancer is overly unlabeled; it does not capture high-grade features or subtype and is less complete than R3.
The small cell diagnosis is weakly supported by NSE and nonspecific poorly differentiated carcinoma; it lacks typical raw small-cell morphology, hypercalcemia, or age features.
Append-only anatomical completion adds no subtype/grade and remains too broad and subordinate to R4.
